claims.excerpt: CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports
claims.claim: The piece concerns the relationship between CPython 3.13 free threading and extension imports.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading, a configuration that can run with the global interpreter lock disabled. An extension must explicitly indicate that it supports this mode; importing one without that declaration warns and enables the GIL.
claims.narrative: Explain how CPython 3.13’s experimental free-threading configuration connects an application’s runtime choice to what happens when it imports an extension.
claims.explanation: The title accurately identifies the subject and scope covered by the source.
